_comment: Static dataset for the Process Memory (dev) report -- the 'Who holds the memory'
Nothing here comes from this repo's autoplay stats DB. The figures are one-off
measurements of a live CivilizationV_DX11.exe taken in the Community-Patch-DLL
workspace: the DLL's own allocation hook (MemHookTags), the heap walk and
address-space walk it writes to the game's cache/stats.db (MemHeapDetail,
MemHeapSummary, MemAddressSpace), the Lua Tier 2 allocator profile, and a VMMap
capture of a reference game for the items marked est.
All sizes are MB, and the whole 4,096 MB address space is accounted for: every
item's value sums to 'space', which is committed + reserved + free. Reserve whose
owner is known is charged to that owner and counted once (dll.minidump,
dll.hookreserve, drv.reserve), so the rsv.* family is only the reserve that is
shared between owners or unclaimed. Headroom (free.*) is drawn unfilled: it is
the one part of the ring holding nothing.
Fragmentation is a re-partition, not new data: the CRT and Lua heap free lists and the
small free holes are carved out of EXE, Lua and Headroom respectively. Those three owner
totals are therefore SMALLER here than in the published artifact, which folds each into
the owner of the heap. Everything still sums to 'space'.

owners.name: DLL
owners.desc: Vox Populi's CvGameCore_Expansion2.dll: everything it allocates, plus its image

owners.name: Lua
owners.desc: All 69 Lua UI contexts, in Lua's own heap

owners.name: Video driver
owners.desc: Driver and Direct3D memory inside the game process. Not VRAM

owners.name: EXE
owners.desc: The EXE and everything else: engine, Windows, Steam, and memory with no known owner

owners.name: Reserved
owners.desc: Address space claimed but never committed, and with no owner we can name

owners.name: Fragmentation
owners.desc: Address space the process cannot put to work: allocator free lists that hold no data, and free holes too small to serve a real allocation

owners.name: Headroom
owners.desc: Address space nobody has claimed. The only part of the ring holding nothing — and the part that runs out

items.label: DLL code and static data
items.desc: The loaded CvGameCore_Expansion2.dll image

items.label: Game database tables
items.desc: XML info tables loaded at startup (tag XmlDatabaseLoad); identical in both games

items.label: Map generation
items.desc: Left over from generating a fresh map (tag MapGeneration)

items.label: Map, pathfinder pools and statics
items.desc: Allocations outside any tagged scope, mostly made before turn 1

items.label: Danger plots
items.desc: Per-player, per-plot danger maps and the small vectors inside them

items.label: Loaded-save data
items.desc: Allocated while reading a save (tag Serialization); a fresh game has none

items.label: AI subsystems
items.desc: Tactical, homeland, economic, military and diplomacy AI, and the tactical analysis map

items.label: Turn processing and pathfinding
items.desc: Player and city turn processing, and the pathfinder

items.label: Diagnostics hook tables
items.desc: The allocation hook's own side table. Instrumented builds only

items.label: Minidump emergency reserve
items.desc: 16 MB reserved at startup so the crash handler can still write a dump when memory has run out. Reserved, never committed

items.label: Hook node pool, unused part
items.desc: The reserved tail of the hook's 32 MB node pool, which commits in 1 MB steps as it fills. Instrumented builds only

items.label: VPUI GameInfo cache
items.desc: VPUI_core.lua, almost all of it line 71: database rows materialised into Lua tables

items.label: EUI table cache
items.desc: EUI_core_library.lua, mostly line 418: a never-evicting copy of database rows

items.label: Tooltip builder
items.desc: InfoTooltipInclude.lua

items.label: Other UI scripts
items.desc: About 200 other scripts, none above 1.3 MB

items.label: Objects built by engine code
items.desc: Lua objects created by C code with no script on the stack

items.label: Lua objects, not profiled
items.desc: No per-script profile exists for this game; on the small map two caches held 70%

items.label: NVIDIA driver code
items.desc: nvgpucomp32, nvd3dum, nvwgf2um and helper DLLs

items.label: Direct3D and DXGI runtime
items.desc: d3d11, dxgi and related system DLLs

items.label: GPU-mapped buffers
items.desc: Write-combined private memory: the driver's CPU-visible GPU buffers. 44–66 MB across the reference captures

items.label: NVIDIA shader cache
items.desc: The memory-mapped .nvph cache file

items.label: Driver buffer reserve
items.desc: The reserved part of the driver's write-combined GPU buffer regions

items.label: Civ 5 EXE
items.desc: CivilizationV_DX11.exe; 86 MB of it is the .data section

items.label: Engine blocks of 1 MB or more
items.desc: Renderer transform buffers, pattern-filled and zeroed buffers, file-read staging

items.label: Engine blocks under 1 MB
items.desc: CRT heap blocks the hook did not record. Measured directly: the EXE's, not the DLL's

items.label: Engine pool heap
items.desc: One ~58 MB structured block and ~700 small ones

items.label: Windows process heap
items.desc: Windows, the Direct3D runtime, the driver and Steam, mixed together

items.label: Windows, Steam and other DLLs
items.desc: Every loaded image except the EXE, driver, Direct3D and VP DLL. Steam is 24.5 MB of it

items.label: Unnamed private memory
items.desc: VirtualAlloc'd memory outside any heap, owner unknown. May include heap bookkeeping the walk misses

items.label: Small heaps, shared sections, stacks, OS files
items.desc: ~25 MB in small heaps, ~30 MB shared sections, ~8 MB thread stacks and TEBs, ~8 MB locale and resource files

items.label: CRT heap segment reserve
items.desc: Address space the shared CRT heap owns and has not committed. It cannot be split between the DLL and the engine

items.label: Heap 10 segment reserve
items.desc: One unidentified Win32 heap reserves ~73 MB in both games to hold ~14 MB of data

items.label: Other heap segment reserve
items.desc: The Windows process heap, Lua's heap and a dozen small heaps

items.label: Unowned 128 MB reservation
items.desc: A single reservation at 0x10020000 with 0.6 MB committed. Nothing has claimed it

items.label: Thread stack reserve
items.desc: 146 stack regions for ~73 threads: 48.6 MB reserved, only 6.4 MB of it ever committed

items.label: Shared sections and image tails
items.desc: Reserved parts of shareable sections and of mapped images

items.label: Unattributed reservations
items.desc: Reserved address space with no owner identified: the residual after everything above

items.label: CRT heap free lists and overhead
items.desc: Committed inside the CRT heap the DLL and the engine share, holding no data. Only that heap can reuse it, and only for a matching size

items.label: Lua heap free lists and overhead
items.desc: The same, inside Lua's own heap: committed, and not holding objects

items.label: Free holes too small to use
items.desc: 478 holes at turn 7, 623 at turn 344, none of them the largest. Free, but not to an allocation of any size that matters

items.label: Largest free block
items.desc: What a single allocation can still be given
